profiles.meeting_scenario: The meeting is a 30-minute coordination check between the backend repair pipeline and the human-validation portal teams for CodeR3's first internal pilot. Context: the team plans to hand off three revived legacy Taverna workflows—"Alzheimer pathway enrichment," "Arabidopsis microarray normalization," and "Marine metagenomics taxonomy lookup"—from the GenAI conversion pipeline into the crowdsourcing validation portal ahead of a Friday demo. Agenda: confirm which workflow packages are being handed over, what content each handoff package contains, how those packages reach the portal staging area, and what status counts as being ready for reviewers. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on a Thursday handoff of the pilot workflows, the bundle contents, and the staging process for reviewer onboarding.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.role: Backend Platform Lead, Workflow Repair Pipeline
members.expertise: Workflow orchestration, artifact packaging, legacy system ingestion, Snakemake-based execution infrastructure
members.background: Priya previously maintained bioinformatics workflow infrastructure at a research institute and now leads CodeR3's pipeline that parses Taverna workflows, generates repaired workflow artifacts, and emits machine-readable conversion metadata.
members.private_state: Priya wants the pilot to demonstrate that the repair pipeline can operate with minimal manual intervention, and she is trying to avoid her team becoming responsible for reviewer-facing curation work that could slow future scaling.
hidden_assumptions: A workflow is "ready for validation" once the generated Snakemake or VisFlow package exists, the manifest is complete, and at least one dry-run succeeds on the fixture dataset.
When people use a case-study name like "the Alzheimer workflow," they mean the latest normalized snapshot in the frozen imports directory rather than an earlier raw Taverna export or portal record.
Including "provenance" in a handoff package means shipping machine-readable conversion logs, substitution JSON, and execution metadata, not explanatory notes written for reviewers.
Putting a package in "staging" means uploading a versioned bundle to the artifact bucket that downstream services monitor, not manually registering it inside the portal.

members.name: Daniel Kim
members.role: Validation Experience Lead, Human-in-the-Loop Review Portal
members.expertise: Reviewer workflows, QA tooling, annotation interfaces, research software usability
members.background: Daniel has built internal review and adjudication tools for data-centric platforms and now leads the CodeR3 portal where community validators inspect revived workflows, compare outputs, and record approval decisions.
members.private_state: Daniel needs reviewers to be able to start work without engineering back-and-forth, and he is worried that thin technical bundles will create blocked review tasks that make the pilot look disorganized.
hidden_assumptions: A workflow is "ready for validation" only when a reviewer can open the case in the portal, see enough context to understand substitutions, and complete a first-pass assessment without asking engineers for clarification.
When people refer to "the Alzheimer workflow," they mean the case already imported into the portal from the original public Taverna export, because that is the identifier reviewers and ops are using.
Including "provenance" in a handoff package means providing concise reviewer-facing rationale, visible original-to-substituted service mappings, and enough context to justify suspicious repairs.
Putting a package in "staging" means the item appears in the portal's staging review queue after registration, because that is the only staging surface his team interacts with.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as ready for validation
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say a workflow will be "ready for validation" by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the repair pipeline has produced the revived package, emitted metadata, and completed an automated dry-run on fixture data.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means reviewers can open the case in the portal with enough context and materials to begin a human review immediately.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a routine status label, and both participants commonly use it in cross-team updates without unpacking whether it refers to backend completion or reviewer usability.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Alzheimer workflow instance they mean
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to "the Alzheimer workflow" as if it is a single shared artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is thinking of the latest frozen April snapshot that the converter normalized and reran after repairing service references.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the portal case imported earlier from the original public Taverna export that reviewers already saw in last week's test.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The workflow title is the same across multiple nearby artifacts, and each participant mostly works within their own system's canonical copy, so the name feels specific enough even though it is not.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included when they say provenance
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the bundle should "include provenance."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes provenance includes machine-oriented conversion logs, the substitution map JSON, prompt traces, and execution metadata generated by the repair pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes provenance includes reviewer-facing summaries of why each service was replaced, visible links between original and substituted steps, and compact explanatory context inside the portal.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see provenance as an obviously required part of the package, but each silently includes different layers of material in that label based on their team's downstream use.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say Priya will "put it in staging" on Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya plans to upload versioned bundles to the artifact bucket that the integration jobs consume overnight.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes the workflows will show up in the portal's staging review queue, either because they are directly registered there or because that is what staging means operationally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The teams use the same term for adjacent parts of the deployment chain, and each person's usual tools hide the intermediate handoff steps, making the phrase feel safely unambiguous.

turns.inner_thought: We have all three pilot workflows nearly through packaging: Alzheimer pathway enrichment, Arabidopsis microarray normalization, and Marine metagenomics taxonomy lookup. What I need from this meeting is confirmation that Thursday means my team can hand off versioned repaired bundles after the nightly run, not get dragged into reviewer prep or ad hoc explanations. If the manifests are complete and the dry-runs land, that is enough to call them ready on my side.

turns.inner_thought: For Friday, I mainly care that reviewers can actually begin work without chasing engineering. The Alzheimer workflow is the one they've already seen in the portal, so that has to be ready for validation by Thursday in the reviewer sense, and I'd like the other cases in good enough shape to assign if possible. If Thursday only means backend artifacts exist, we'll get blocked tasks.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's still the target. From the review side, the main thing is that the Alzheimer workflow and ideally the other two are ready for validation by Thursday so we can line up Friday assignments.

turns.inner_thought: The Alzheimer workflow is already stable on the latest frozen April snapshot in imports; tonight's regeneration should just refresh the repaired package and metadata. Assuming the dry-run still passes on fixtures, it's ready for validation. I should keep this framed at the usual status level so we don't reopen scope around manual curation.
turns.utterance: That should be fine. The Alzheimer workflow is already looking stable on our side, and after tonight's regeneration run I expect it to be ready for validation.

turns.inner_thought: Good. What I really need is provenance that helps a reviewer understand the substitutions in the case they open in the portal, especially anything that will look suspicious at first glance. If they can see why the GeoNames replacement happened, they won't stall before even starting comparisons.
turns.utterance: Great. As long as the bundle includes provenance, reviewers should be able to understand why the GeoNames service was substituted before they start comparing steps.

turns.inner_thought: That's already covered. The converter emits conversion logs, substitution map JSON, prompt traces, and replay/execution metadata for every repaired step. Provenance is one of the easier boxes for me to check because it's generated automatically; I definitely do not want this to turn into writing reviewer notes.
turns.utterance: Yes, provenance will be in the bundle. The converter already emits that material for every repaired step, so it should come across with the package.

turns.inner_thought: Once they're in staging, my team can treat them as live pre-review cases: attach them to the portal queue, preload screens, and get reviewer assignments set. I'm assuming staging means they'll appear where ops and reviewers expect them, not just exist somewhere upstream.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Then once the workflows are in staging, my team can attach them to the portal queue and preload the reviewer screens.

turns.inner_thought: Right, I'll put the versioned bundles into the artifact bucket after the nightly build. The downstream integration jobs should pick them up before morning if nothing flakes. That's the standard staging handoff; I don't need to say more unless there's an issue.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll put the versioned bundles in staging right after the nightly build so downstream jobs can pick them up before morning.

turns.inner_thought: I want to make sure the VisFlow preview that shows up for reviewers corresponds to the Alzheimer workflow case already in the portal, since that is the one from last week's dry run and the identifier the ops team has been using. If the preview points somewhere else under the same name, people will think they are seeing the same case when they aren't.
turns.utterance: One detail on the VisFlow side: will the preview point at the Alzheimer workflow already in the portal record so reviewers are looking at the same case they saw in last week's dry run?

turns.inner_thought: The preview will use the current normalized Alzheimer package and its manifest from the latest frozen snapshot, not an older raw export. That should be fine because it's the current package. And if the dry-run passed, it's ready for validation by our normal criteria, so I don't see a blocker here.
turns.utterance: The preview will use the current Alzheimer package and its manifest, and I assume that still counts as ready for validation if the dry-run passed.

turns.inner_thought: Okay, then I'll tell the reviewer group to expect the Thursday staging drop, with provenance included, and plan for first-pass review Friday morning. I’m taking this as meaning the cases will be available in the portal queue with enough context to start immediately, so this should let us avoid last-minute scrambling.
